title: Drone holding its altitude with a PID controller (up and down only)
assumptions: the drone moves only up and down
thrust changes instantly and stays between 0 N and the motors' maximum
maximum thrust is the thrust-to-weight ratio times the base drone's weight; a payload adds weight, not thrust
air drag is a straight-line rule; the lesson's value is exaggerated so the bounce dies out quickly
the D term acts on the measured speed, not on the change in error
the I term stops adding while thrust is at a limit and the error pushes further past it (clamping anti-windup)
wind is a downward push for a set time, or steady
the drone starts at rest on the ground; settling time is given only when the run settled (within 2% of the final height, staying there)
fixed 2 ms steps (semi-implicit Euler), 15 s per run
excludes: a hover-thrust estimate and nested control loops
settings for tuning a real drone

worked_examples.location: packages/solvers/src/pidAltitude.test.ts: steady-state gap m·g/Kp (P only, P + D, heavier drone, steady wind) and the linear stability limit (Kd + c)·Kp > m·Ki (Routh–Hurwitz); hand derivations, not textbook
